In the present study, we applied this enrichment approach to poultry manure to examine how β-lactamase-resistant antibiotics (cefotaxime and meropenem) shape the composition and resistance profiles of copiotrophic, gut-like microbial community relative to an earlier β-lactam (ampicillin) and to antibiotic-free controls. Our results show that extended-spectrum and last-resort β-lactams induced more pronounced shifts in microbial diversity, resistome, and mobilome profiles compared to ampicillin. When focusing on specific taxa, such as clinically relevant enteric bacteria and both susceptible and β-lactam-resistant coliforms, differential responses were observed correlating to the antimicrobial range of action. Moreover, cefotaxime and meropenem exerted different effects on the relative abundance of enteric bacteria and plasmids harboring multiple ARGs. Together, these findings underline how the diversity of pathogen and AMR indicators in gut microbiomes may be shaped by different selective pressures imposed by β-lactamase-resistant antibiotics.IMPORTANCEThis study explores how different generations of β-lactam antibiotics shape microbial communities and antibiotic resistance in a gut-likesystem. Using a metabolically driven synthetic community derived from manure, we found that advanced β-lactams such as cefotaxime and meropenem led to stronger and more specific shifts in both community composition and resistance gene profiles compared to ampicillin. These results emphasize that the ecological impact of antibiotics depends not only on whether bacteria are inhibited but also on the spectrum of activity of each compound. In addition, the system we used provides a simple and controllable way to study interactions among antibiotics, microbial communities, and the resistome. Overall, this work offers a clearer ecological view of how clinically important antibiotics may influence microbiomes and the spread of antibiotic resistance genes.

title: Genomic insights into non-tuberculous mycobacteria isolated from patients in a Chinese hospital
abstract: Non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) are increasingly recognized as important opportunistic pathogens, yet the genomic basis of their antimicrobial resistance and virulence in clinical settings remains incompletely understood. We performed whole-genome sequencing on 28 clinical isolates of NTM collected from Chinese patients (primarily bronchoalveolar lavage fluid) between 2022 and 2025, combined with broth microdilution susceptibility testing and comprehensive bioinformatics analysis. The collection comprised diverse species, including,,,,,,, and. Phenotypic testing revealed extensive multidrug resistance: 100% of isolates were resistant to rifampicin, erythromycin, imipenem, and doxycycline; 82.1% were resistant to ciprofloxacin; 89.3% were resistant to linezolid; and only amikacin retained substantial activity (50% susceptible). Resistome profiling using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database/Resistance Gene Identifier identified heterogeneous distributions of efflux pumps (tap), ribosomal methylases [Erm(39)], β-lactamases (blaF), and other determinants, consistent with both intrinsic and accessory-genome-mediated resistance. Virulence factor annotation against the Virulence Factor Database revealed 531 unique factors, with hierarchical clustering separating isolates into two major clades: (i) rapid-growing species (and) enriched in secretion systems (ESX/T7SS), polyketide synthases, and lipid biosynthesis genes, and (ii) slow-growingcomplex species showing lower overall virulence gene abundance. Pangenome analysis indicated a relatively closed pangenome structure, with 1,026 core genes and substantial shell/cloud compartments contributing to strain-specific adaptations. These findings provide genomic insights into the multidrug-resistant and virulence-heterogeneous nature of contemporary Chinese clinical isolates of NTM.IMPORTANCEIn this study, we sequenced 28 clinical non-tuberculous mycobacterial strains, performed comprehensive drug susceptibility testing, and analyzed virulence factors to elucidate genomic determinants of resistance and pathogenicity, as well as evolutionary characteristics. These findings aim to bridge existing knowledge gaps, informing improved diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for non-tuberculous mycobacterial infections.

title: Antimicrobial Resistance Trends in COVID-19 Patients with Hospital Infection in Intensive Care: A Retrospective Study in Central Italy, 2020-2022
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) was exacerbated by COVID-19 pandemic. This study describes prevalence and trends of AMR in patients with diagnosed severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection admitted during 2020-2022 to the intensive care unit (ICU) in Molise region, central Italy. A retrospective study was conducted, including patients aged ≥ 18 years with at least one positive bacterial or fungal culture during ICU stay. Data were related to patient demographics, ICU outcomes, healthcare-associated infections, and antimicrobial susceptibility profiles. During the 2020-2022 period, 103 ICU admissions met the inclusion criteria, yielding 268 isolations, of which 157 underwent antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Apart from high proportion of, Gram-negative bacteria predominated, with,,, andamong the most frequent. Resistance to beta-lactams and carbapenems was consistently high, while it ranged from 53.8% to 66.7% to fluoroquinolones and remained above 50% to aminoglycosides. Tetracycline resistance showed significant year-to-year variation, increasing in 2022 compared with both 2020 and 2021. AMR rates in COVID-19 patients in ICU were persistently high throughout the pandemic, with critical resistance levels in Gram-negatives, underlining the need to reinforce infection prevention and control measures and antimicrobial stewardship programs and align prescribing practices with World Health Organization AWaRe recommendations, even during public health emergencies.

title: Hybrid membrane vesicle-enabled sonodynamic therapy using ciprofloxacin for treating biofilm-associated infections
abstract: Biofilm-associated infections on indwelling medical devices pose significant clinical challenges due to antibiotic resistance and poor drug penetration. Sonodynamic therapy (SDT) is a promising strategy utilizing ultrasound to activate sonosensitizers for generating reactive oxygen species (ROS). However, the lack of safe and effective sonosensitizers and bacterial-targeting delivery systems limits its application in treating biofilm infection. To address these limitations, we developed antibiotic ciprofloxacin-loaded hybrid membrane vesicles (CIP@HMVs), where ciprofloxacin acts as a safe sonosensitizer and HMVs serve as a detoxified bacterial-targeted delivery system. HMVs were engineered by fusing-derived outer membrane vesicles (PAEVs) with macrophage membrane vesicles (MMVs), creating a dual-functional nanoplatform with homotypic bacteria-targeting and detoxification capabilities. CIP@HMVs exploited ciprofloxacin's sonosensitizer properties to generate singlet oxygen (O) under ultrasound, while HMVs enhanced bacterial uptake in. This enabled synergistic bactericidal effects against planktonic bacteriamembrane disruption and intracellular ROS burst, achieving a 5.7-log bacterial reduction in catheter biofilms. Crucially, HMVs neutralized PAEVs' LPS toxicityand demonstrated negligible systemic toxicity. In a murine catheter-infection model, CIP@HMVs under ultrasound achieved 99.8% bacterial eradication and reduced inflammation. This bacterial-targeting sonodynamic platform provides a transformative strategy for treating device-associated biofilm infections with high efficacy and biosafety.

title: In silico analysis of SCO, an almost undescribed family of β-lactamases
abstract: β-lactamases rank amongst the most common mechanisms of antibiotic resistance, accounting for thousands of different variants. Current genomic tools have resulted in an exponential growth of new variants, most of which, as is the case for SCO, remain undescribed or non-characterised. This study aimed to detect new variants of SCO in GenBank records. The amino acid sequence of SCO-1 was compared with what is present in GenBank. Only amino acid sequences with >85% identity were considered. No synthetic or partial sequences were included in the analyses. Eleven different SCO variants were detected, 9 of which had previously not been designated as specific variants. Several of the modifications suggested the possible expansion of substrates towards 3rd and 4th generation cephalosporins or the resistance to inhibitors, while others might impair SCO functionality. SCO β-lactamases were detected in 6 bacterial families accounting for 14 genera. The presence of undescribed SCO variants in GenBank is reported, and the need to establish the exact substrate profile of new variants is highlighted.

Genomic dynamics and macrolide resistance in Bordetella pertussis: implications for surveillance and rapid visual detection
abstract: The post-COVID-19 resurgence of pertussis has raised concerns regarding shifts in circulating Bordetella pertussis populations and increasing macrolide resistance. This study aims to characterize the population dynamics and clinically relevant genomic changes of B. pertussis in China and globally, and to develop a rapid visual assay for detecting the macrolide resistance-associated 23S rRNA A2047G mutation. In this cross-sectional genomic epidemiology study, 22 recent clinical isolates were sequenced and analyzed with 7322 publicly available B. pertussis genomes. Global population structure was assessed using 7344 genomes, and Bayesian phylodynamic analysis was performed on 1054 temporally informative Chinese genomes selected from 1292 isolates collected during 1951-2024. We designed and optimized an allele-specific loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assay incorporating a 3'-terminal artificial mismatch and a neutral red indicator for detection of the macrolide resistance-associated 23S rRNA A2047G mutation. Its analytical sensitivity and specificity were evaluated alongside quantitative PCR (qPCR) using serially diluted plasmids and 39 contrived DNA samples. The macrolide resistance of B. pertussis in China, defined by the 23S rRNA A2047G mutation, reached 98.9% (88/89; 95% CI 93.9-100) among available genomes in 2024, concurrent with the rapid clonal expansion of the ptxP3-MT28 sub-lineage. Among the available Chinese isolates, the proportion of predicted Prn-deficient strains increased to 31.46% in 2024, with 12 distinct prn inactivation mechanisms, predominantly IS481-mediated insertions. The optimized LAMP assay differentiated mutant and wild-type alleles within 50 min at 65°C, with a neutral red visual limit of detection (LOD) of 10 copies/μL, compared with 100 copies/μL for qPCR. The results of LAMP-based differentiation were consistent with those obtained by qPCR for all 39 contrived samples. B. pertussis populations have undergone marked genomic shifts characterized by antigenic variation and macrolide resistance, although the evolutionary drivers underlying these temporal and genomic patterns remain to be determined. The visual LAMP assay provides a proof-of-concept analytical evidence for rapid A2047G allele discrimination and may have future point-of-care potential following validation with prospective clinical respiratory specimens. These findings support continued genomic surveillance and further evaluation of vaccine antigen matching and antimicrobial resistance.

title: Integrated profiling of β-lactam susceptibility and spoilage-associated enzyme activities in psychrotrophic bacteria from the raw milk production chain
abstract: Psychrotrophic bacteria are important targets for microbiological control of cold-chain raw milk because of their ability to produce spoilage-associated enzymes and harbor antimicrobial resistance determinants. However, these two functional characteristics are often investigated separately, leaving their co-occurrence within the same isolate collection insufficiently characterized. To address this gap, 543 dominant culturable bacterial isolates were recovered from raw milk and dairy-farm-associated samples collected from six regions of China. Pseudomonas was the most prevalent genus, followed by Acinetobacter, Chryseobacterium, Serratia, and Psychrobacter. β-Lactam minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) distributions varied substantially among genera, with Chryseobacterium exhibiting the highest proportion of β-lactamase-associated phenotype-positive isolates. Among 226 raw-milk isolates screened using ceftazidime, all 44 isolates showing inhibitor-responsive or carbapenemase-associated phenotypes were subjected to whole-genome sequencing. Genome-wide resistance-gene screening identified annotated β-lactamase genes predominantly in Chryseobacterium and Acinetobacter. In contrast, the resistance-related annotations retained in phenotype-positive Pseudomonas isolates were mainly associated with efflux systems and adaptive response mechanisms. In the integrated analysis, a relative MIC-enzyme risk-prioritization score ranked Serratia (0.88), Chryseobacterium (0.71), and Pseudomonas (0.67) as the three highest-ranking genera. The β-lactam MIC score showed weak positive correlations with the protease-associated score (Spearman's ρ = 0.297, P < 0.001) and with the lipase-associated score (ρ = 0.194, P < 0.001). These findings indicate that genus abundance alone is insufficient to characterize the functional heterogeneity of psychrotrophic bacteria in raw milk. Integrating β-lactam MIC patterns with spoilage-enzyme activity provides complementary information for genus-level prioritization within this isolate collection.

title: Occurrence, distribution, and risks of antibiotics in mollusks from the coast of South China
abstract: To assess the contamination status and health risks of antibiotics in mollusks from South China, this study investigated the enrichment characteristics of 20 antibiotics in 104 mollusk samples collected from 15 coastal cities. Among the mollusk samples analyzed, Guangdong Province exhibited the highest total antibiotic concentration (Σ20Antibiotics), ranging from 45.70 to 343.9 ng gdry weight (dw), with a mean value of 143.1 ng gdw. β-Lactam and tetracycline antibiotics were identified as the predominant classes. A positive correlation was observed between the trophic level of mollusks and the concentrations of these two antibiotic classes. All trophic magnification factors (TMFs) exceeded 1, indicating potential biomagnification of β-lactam and tetracycline antibiotics within mollusks. Both carcinogenic and non-carcinogenic health risks posed by antibiotic residues in mollusks to consumers were at acceptably low levels. Nevertheless, the dissemination risk of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) resulting from antibiotic pollution remains a persistent potential health threat warranting continued vigilance.

title: Salinity-dependent effects of erythromycin on biofilm development and conjugative plasmid transfer on poly(vinyl chloride) microplastics
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) and antibiotics frequently co-occur in aquatic environments and jointly influence the dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). However, the modulatory role of salinity, a highly dynamic factor in estuarine and coastal regions, remains underexplored. This study investigated the effects of erythromycin (ERY) on biofilm development and RP4 plasmid conjugative transfer on poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) MPs across varying salinity levels (5‰, 10‰, and 15‰). Results demonstrated that MP hydrophobicity increased with salinity, while the ERY adsorption capacity followed the order: 5‰ > 15‰ > 10‰. A higher salinity (15‰) promoted biofilm biomass and extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) secretion on MPs. Notably, conjugative transfer frequencies within MP-associated biofilms were consistently higher than those in planktonic cultures. Under varying salinities, the conjugation frequencies in biofilms displayed a U-shaped trend, with higher rates observed at 5‰ and 15‰ compared to 10‰. Crucially, the impact of ERY on plasmid transfer was highly salinity-dependent, i.e., the addition of ERY promoted conjugation at 5‰ and 10‰ but significantly inhibited it at 15‰. Physiological assessments revealed that exposure to varying salinities and ERY induced non-lethal oxidative stress, evidenced by elevated reactive oxygen species and upregulated antioxidant enzymes (CAT and SOD), while lipid peroxidation (MDA) remained relatively low. Concurrently, intracellular proline accumulation and cell membrane permeability increased significantly with rising salinity. These findings provide direct experimental evidence that salinity fluctuations and antibiotic residues jointly alter bacterial physiological states and antibiotic resistance dissemination on MPs, which highlights the necessity of considering dynamic environmental variables in ecological risk assessments.

Concentration-dependent impacts of ofloxacin on the mobilization-immobilization dynamics of geogenic arsenic in groundwater environment
abstract: Arsenic (As) behaviors in aquifers can be altered by exogenetic antibiotics and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), which modifies evolution of originally geogenic As-contaminated groundwater while increasing environmental risk of ARGs. The roles of introduced antibiotics in As biogeochemical cycle in groundwater environments however remain elusive mechanistically. Using Shewanella oneidensis (S. oneidensis) as a model, this research elucidates the impacts of varying levels of antibiotic (e.g., ofloxacin) exposure on As fate during microbially-mediated reductive dissolution of host goethite. Under low-level ofloxacin exposure (≤1 μg/L), S. oneidensis restored secretion of riboflavin after a short period of stress adaptation. Conversely, high ofloxacin exposure (≥10 μg/L) consistently depleted aqueous riboflavin and weakened mineral-biomolecule interactions, restricting electron transfer and inhibiting goethite bioreduction. Contrasting changes in the abundances of ARGs (e.g., qnrA) and As efflux gene (e.g., arsB) indicate concentration-dependent reorganization of resistance-associated genetic potential under ofloxacin and As co-exposure, while aqueous As(III) accumulated despite declining arsB abundance. Therefore, the molecular mechanism underlying As migration differs depending upon antibiotic exposure levels. These findings provide novel insights into underestimated effects of concomitant antibiotics on As re-mobilization in geogenic contaminated groundwater.

title: Nationwide Survey of Antimicrobial Stewardship in Korean Hospitals: Insights From the Early Stage of the 2024 National Pilot Implementation
